en: The Eight Verses on the Bilva Tree (Bilvāṣṭaka)
The single bilva leaf offered to Śiva—possessing three lobes, the form of the three qualities (guṇas), three eyes, and the three weapons; which destroys the sins of the three births—is [supreme].
With auspicious, tender, and flawless bilva leaves having three branches...
I shall perform worship to you alone...
2. The sight of bilva trees and their touch destroy sin;
the [mantra] of Aghora destroys all evil—[to you] alone... 3.
In Śālagrāma stones, in Brahmins, in a pond, and in forest wells,
[the merit] is equal to thousands of crores of sacrifices.
In thousands of crores of elephant tusks and hundreds of horse-sacrifices, [the merit is likewise].
By the gift of ten million maidens, one...
5. And by [offering] even a single *bilva* leaf, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices;
for the sake of worshipping Mahādeva, one... 6.
Dwelling in the sacred field of Kāśī and beholding Kālabhairava;
having seen [the Lord] at Gayā and Prayāga...
7 ...the Lord of Gods together with Umā, and Nandin, the bull-vehicle of Śaṅkara.
One is liberated from all sins by offering even a single bilva fruit to Śiva.
Thus ends the Śrī Bilvāṣṭaka.
Tulasī, Bilva, Nirguṇḍī, Apāmārga, Kapittha,
Śamī, Āmalaka, and Dūrvā are proclaimed as the eight bilvas.
Thus ends [the section on] the eight bilvas.
